protocol.instrument_name: Protocol for Management of Urinary Tract Infections for Tasmanian Pharmacists
protocol.instrument_version: Version 2.0 (cover: 'Version 2.0 May 2025'; version history: 'V 2.0 May 2025 ... Legislative change'; V1.0 April 2024 Original Protocol)
protocol.effective_date: May 2025 (cover and version history); authority table records authorisation by Dale Webster, Secretary, Department of Health on 4 June 2025
protocol.legal_basis: Tasmanian Poisons Regulations 2018 Regulation 7(4) (Relevant Legislation, page 3-4): '(4) A pharmacist, in the lawful practice of the pharmacist's profession, may possess, sell, supply or prescribe any scheduled substance in accordance with a protocol authorised by the Secretary, that specifically authorises the possession, sale, supply or prescription of that substance by a pharmacist. This protocol has been endorsed by the Secretary.' Authorisation Statement (page 2): 'In accordance with Tasmanian Poisons Regulations 2018 Regulation 7(4) - I authorise this protocol.' (Dale Webster, Secretary). About (page 3): 'A change to the Poisons Regulations 2018 allows pharmacists to supply medications included in this protocol.' and 'It is a regulatory requirement under the Tasmanian Poison Regulations 2018 that pharmacists follow this protocol under a structured prescribing arrangement.'
protocol.supervision_model: Structured prescribing arrangement (Glossary, page 3: 'prescribing specific medications for a specified purpose in accordance with a protocol published by the Tasmanian Department of Health'). Mandatory Requirements (page 3): 'Hold a general registration as a pharmacist with Pharmacy Board of Australia (AHPRA). - Prescribe medications as published in this protocol and produce and retain records of consultations and prescribing. - Retain evidence of completion of one of the training courses listed in this authorised protocol. - Maintain and retain evidence of continuing professional development - relevant to scope of practice. - Work in a pharmacy premises that is approved for extended scope activities.' Service must only be offered 'in a pharmacy premises that has been approved for this purpose by the Department of Health' (About, page 3).
protocol.scope_summary: Tasmanian Department of Health authorised protocol for community pharmacists to assess and treat suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infections. Sequential flowchart (pages 5-7): immediate pyelonephritis/sepsis screen with Emergency Department referral; sex, age 18-65 (inclusive) and consent gates; symptom-count gate (2 or more of pain with urination, urinary frequency, urinary urgency, suprapubic pain); alternative-condition check; two diversion boxes (co-morbidity/anatomical exclusion box with 'Immediate GP referral'; recurrent-UTI box with 'Refer to GP'); and a multi-resistant/STI risk-factor box that diverts to symptom-relief treatment with mandatory GP referral (antibiotics 'may be supplied if pharmacist considers clinically appropriate'). Provisional diagnosis of uncomplicated UTI leads to over-the-counter symptom relief, self-care advice and first/second/third-line antibiotics (trimethoprim, nitrofurantoin, cefalexin), dispensing and labelling per Poisons Regulations 2018, follow-up advice, documentation/GP record sharing, and post-service contact 3-5 days after the consultation.

inclusion.text: 'What is the sex of the patient?' - the branch 'Female or patient with unmodified female genital anatomy from birth' continues through the protocol; the branch 'Male or patient with innate variations of sex characteristics (intersex) or patient who has undergone gender reassignment surgery' is routed to 'Provide usual care / Consider offering treatment for symptoms with over-the-counter medicines and self-care advice and/ or refer to GP'.

steps.description: 'Does the patient have any symptoms suggesting pyelonephritis or sepsis?* Fever (higher than 38°C), chills, nausea, vomiting, flank pain, rapid breathing (more than 20 breaths/min), rapid heart rate (higher than 90 bpm), low blood pressure (systolic less than 100 mmHg), new confusion. OR pharmacist has any concern that patient is clinically very unwell or is deteriorating.' Yes -> 'Immediate referral to Emergency Department'. No -> continue to PW-1-S2.

gates.criterion: No symptoms suggesting pyelonephritis or sepsis (no fever >38°C, chills, nausea, vomiting, flank pain, rapid breathing >20 breaths/min, rapid heart rate >90 bpm, systolic BP <100 mmHg, new confusion) and no pharmacist concern that the patient is clinically very unwell or deteriorating

steps.description: 'Provide appropriate antibiotics: - First line - trimethoprim 300 mg orally, daily for 3 days - Second line - nitrofurantoin 100 mg orally, 6-hourly for 5 days Strictly only if trimethoprim and nitrofurantoin cannot be used: - Third line - cefalexin 500 mg orally, 12-hourly for 5 days. Dispense via dispensary software and label according to Poisons Regulations 2018'.

gates.criterion: First-line trimethoprim or second-line nitrofurantoin is usable; third-line cefalexin only when 'trimethoprim and nitrofurantoin cannot be used' (no criteria for 'cannot be used' are printed)

steps.description: 'Provide follow up advice - Symptoms should respond within 48 hours - If symptoms persist 2-3 days after starting treatment, recur within 2 weeks of finishing treatment or symptoms change - patients should be advised to see their GP.'

steps.description: 'Post service follow up - Patients are to be contacted 3 to 5 days after - enquire about ongoing symptoms, medication side effects, provide referral information where appropriate and document follow-up in electronic system. Inform that a voluntary survey will be sent to them via SMS from the Department of Health in the next few days.'

steps.description: 'Document consultation in clinical software and share a record with the patient and their GP.' Page 8 'Documentation requirements:' - 'The pharmacist must make a clinical record of the consultation. It is recommended that the documentation contains - at a minimum: Sufficient information to identify and make contact with the patient; The date of consultation; Name of the pharmacist who undertook the consultation; Documentation of consent given by the patient regarding: costs, pharmacist communication with other healthcare practitioners (e.g. patient's usual treating GP) and access to the patient's My Health Record for checking relevant medical history; Information relevant to the diagnosis or treatment; Clinical opinion reached by the pharmacist; Actions taken by the pharmacist (including any medications supplied or referrals made to a medical practitioner); Details of medications supplied to the patient; Information or advice given to the patient in relation to treatment proposed'. 'The pharmacist should provide a copy of the consultation summary to the patient. The consultation summary is also to be shared with patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice (the only exception to this is if the patient does not have a regular GP or does not consent to their information being shared).'

open_questions.topic: Flowchart pages 5-7: column interleaving in the text extraction
open_questions.observed: Pages 5-7 extract as interleaved question text, Yes/No branch labels and outcome-column text (e.g. 'Yes', 'No', 'Immediate referral to Emergency Department', 'Refer to GP' appear mid-question).
open_questions.why_unclear: Branch-to-action mapping is read best-effort from the linearised flowchart; recorded with confidence 'high' only where the outcome text is unambiguous, 'medium' where mapping could vary (PW-2-S1).

open_questions.topic: No printed section headings on flowchart pages
open_questions.observed: Pages 5-7 carry only the Word template placeholders 'Heading goes here' / 'Subheading follows on here' in their footers; page 5 has no heading above the flowchart, and pages 6-7 begin with the printed line 'Continued from previous page'.
open_questions.why_unclear: section_heading recorded as '' for page 5 content and 'Continued from previous page' for pages 6-7 content; the placeholder text was not used as a heading.

open_questions.topic: Page cross-reference mismatch inside the document
open_questions.observed: Page 4 states 'Pages 4-6 provide an assessment and management protocol for pharmacists for patients presenting with clinical features of a urinary tract infection', but the assessment/management flowchart actually occupies pages 5-7 (treatment and follow-up appear on page 7).
open_questions.why_unclear: Internal page reference appears stale (possibly from v1.0); both the printed statement and the observed flowchart pages are recorded.

open_questions.topic: 'Assess allergies and drug interactions' has no printed branch
open_questions.observed: Page 7 flowchart box: 'Provisional diagnosis for uncomplicated UTI / Assess allergies and drug interactions' then straight on to symptom relief and antibiotics. No Yes/No outcome, threshold or 'refer if contraindicated' instruction is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: Gate recorded with on_fail 'unclear' per spec; no action was invented.

open_questions.observed: 'Strictly only if trimethoprim and nitrofurantoin cannot be used: - Third line - cefalexin 500 mg orally, 12-hourly for 5 days.' The protocol does not define when trimethoprim or nitrofurantoin 'cannot be used' (allergy/interaction assessment is instructed but no rule is given).
open_questions.why_unclear: Restriction transcribed verbatim; gate marked medium confidence with on_fail 'unclear'.

open_questions.topic: Eligibility combinatorics inferred from flowchart sequence
open_questions.observed: The document does not state combinatorics in words. The flowchart is sequential (each question must be answered Yes/No to advance); the exclusion box is explicitly 'Does the patient meet any of the following' (any_of).
open_questions.why_unclear: Inclusion criteria encoded as all_of (sequential AND gates) per spec default; the exclusion boxes are encoded as explicit any_of groups because the document says 'any of the following'.

open_questions.topic: Dual reading of the page 7 risk-factor branch
open_questions.observed: 'Treat using symptom relief and self care advice - antibiotics may be supplied if pharmacist considers clinically appropriate. Always refer these patients to GP even if treatment is provided by pharmacist.' sits on the Yes branch of the risk-factor question, while the No branch reaches 'Provisional diagnosis for uncomplicated UTI'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Patients in this branch are simultaneously diverted from the standard pathway (eligibility gate INC-8), subject to mandatory GP referral (RF-32 to RF-40) and still potentially eligible for antibiotic supply (exclusion exception EXE-1). All three readings recorded; none reconciled away.

open_questions.topic: No quantity-to-supply, max dose or lactation/paediatric caveat printed for antibiotics
open_questions.observed: The protocol prints only strength, route, frequency and duration for trimethoprim, nitrofurantoin and cefalexin. No supply quantity, no max daily dose, no breastfeeding/lactation warning and no paediatric caveat appear anywhere (patients are restricted to 18-65 years).
open_questions.why_unclear: Absence recorded so downstream consumers do not assume values exist; treatment rows carry empty quantity_to_supply/max_dose.

open_questions.topic: Asterisk footnote not present in the extraction
open_questions.observed: 'Does the patient have any symptoms suggesting pyelonephritis or sepsis?*' carries an asterisk but no footnote text appears anywhere on page 5 in the extraction.
open_questions.why_unclear: Footnote content (if any) is not recoverable from the text layer.

open_questions.observed: Referral destinations/criteria appear across pages 5, 6 and 7; the shared provenance object for the referral block uses the first page (5), which has no printed heading (section_heading '').
open_questions.why_unclear: Spec allows one shared provenance for the block; per-item page numbers are annotated inline in each referral string.

open_questions.topic: 'and/ or refer to GP' optionality in the usual-care branches
open_questions.observed: Sex, age and consent branch outcomes read 'Consider offering treatment for symptoms with over-the-counter medicines and self-care advice and/ or refer to GP'.
open_questions.why_unclear: 'and/or' leaves referral optional; the document does not say when referral is required, so no mandatory referral rule was encoded for these branches.

open_questions.observed: The pyelonephritis/sepsis box is one question with an 'OR' across nine symptoms plus a pharmacist-judgement clause; it is encoded as nine separate structured/qualitative red flags (RF-1 to RF-10) all leading to 'Immediate referral to Emergency Department'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Document says 'any symptoms suggesting pyelonephritis or sepsis' (OR semantics); per-item encoding preserves that semantics but multiplies the red-flag count.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'The protocol will not cover all possible clinical circumstances and pharmacists are required to exercise their professional judgement in adapting the treatment guideline to individual circumstances.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Open-ended professional-judgement clause; needs a local policy boundary before it can be enforced by a rules engine.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Mandatory Requirements (page 3): AHPRA general registration, prescribing/record retention as published, evidence of one approved training course, CPD evidence, and working in 'a pharmacy premises that is approved for extended scope activities'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Per-pharmacist and per-premises attestations must be verified before go-live; the document does not state expiry or audit process.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Strictly only if trimethoprim and nitrofurantoin cannot be used' before third-line cefalexin, with no printed criteria for 'cannot be used'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: A hard prescribing restriction with undefined conditions; local policy must define acceptable reasons (allergy, interaction, other) and evidence capture.

hugh_to_confirm.item: '- Assess allergies and drug interactions' with no printed branch or action on a positive finding.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Behaviour when an allergy/interaction blocks first or second line is undefined in the protocol; local rule required (including when to refer).

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Treat using symptom relief and self care advice - antibiotics may be supplied if pharmacist considers clinically appropriate. Always refer these patients to GP even if treatment is provided by pharmacist.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Antibiotic supply on this branch is a pure clinician-judgement clause; local policy must define the boundary and confirm mandatory GP referral is captured.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Consider offering treatment for symptoms with over-the-counter medicines and self-care advice and/ or refer to GP' for patients outside the flowchart scope (sex, age 18-65, consent branches).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Usual care' and the optional 'and/or refer to GP' are undefined; local policy must specify what is provided and when referral becomes mandatory.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Dispense via dispensary software and label according to Poisons Regulations 2018'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Quantity-to-supply and label content are not printed in the protocol; must be configured in local dispensing software within Reg 45/labelling requirements.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'accessing a patient's MyHealth Record is highly recommended' when checking the exclusion box, plus My Health Record consent documented at consultation.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Highly recommended' is not mandatory and depends on local system access and patient consent.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Approved training programs: 'Pharmaceutical Society of Australia - Managing uncomplicated cystitis (Urinary Tract Infection)' and 'Australasian College of Pharmacy (Tasmania) - Uncomplicated Cystitis Treatment - Pharmacist Training'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Approved course lists change; confirm each pharmacist's certificate against the current approved list before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'This protocol will be updated every two years or more frequently as required.'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Version pinning: confirm the module runs against v2.0 (May 2025) and has a re-verification trigger on republication.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Inform that a voluntary survey will be sent to them via SMS from the Department of Health in the next few days' and the 3-5 day post service contact requirement.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Depends on an external departmental SMS/survey system; confirm the local process that evidences contact was made within 3-5 days.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'The consultation summary is also to be shared with patient's usual treating medical practitioner or medical practice (the only exception to this is if the patient does not have a regular GP or does not consent to their information being shared).'
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Notification duty depends on consent and GP nomination; local workflow (and secure transfer method) must be confirmed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: 'Consider pharmacist-initiated treatment of vaginal thrush or GP referral for other causes (skin conditions, bacterial vaginosis)'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Thrush treatment sits outside this protocol's antibiotic scope; confirm the separate thrush-treatment protocol that governs it.
